questions.text: Which source family should control a solar PV interconnection question?

options.text: The Philippine Electrical Code, especially Article 6.90 for PV system scope, disconnects, grounding, plaques, and points of connection.
The plumbing code because PV modules are usually near roof drains.
A history source because solar panels change the building appearance.
Only the DOE energy guideline, with no electrical-code coordination.

questions.rationale: The Philippine Electrical Code, especially Article 6.90 for PV system scope, disconnects, grounding, plaques, and points of connection. PEC Article 6.90 is the checked local source for PV electrical-system requirements.
questions.explanation: 50 mA is a higher threshold used in dry locations, not wet locations where more stringent protection is required. 75 mA exceeds the safe protection level for wet locations and would not comply with PEC requirements. 100 mA is far too high for wet location protection and violates electrical safety standards. The Philippine Electrical Code (PEC), based on NEC/NFPA 70 standards, specifies that electrical fault current protection in wet locations must not exceed 30 mA (less than 30 mA). This lower threshold in wet locations provides enhanced protection against electrical shock hazards where moisture is present, reducing the time delay for circuit disconnection in fault conditions. Wet locations (bathrooms, outdoor) require <30 mA fault current protection per PEC; this is a critical numerical standard for electrical safety.

questions.text: Which source family should control plans for a plumbing installation permit?

options.text: The Revised National Plumbing Code, including RMP-signed plans, administrative review, inspection, and testing.
PEC Article 6.90 because all utility systems use service entrances.
A UAP fee schedule with no plumbing-code review.
Only the DOE lighting-power-density rules.

questions.rationale: The Revised National Plumbing Code, including RMP-signed plans, administrative review, inspection, and testing. The plumbing code locators state the permit, plan, review, inspection, testing, and Registered Master Plumber requirements.
questions.explanation: 5 lux is insufficient for safe evacuation and does not meet regulatory requirements. 20 lux exceeds the minimum required standard; while acceptable, 10 lux is the baseline threshold. 30 lux is above the minimum emergency lighting requirement. The Philippine Electrical Code (PEC) Part 7 establishes that emergency lighting systems must maintain a minimum illumination level of 10 lux throughout evacuation routes and exit areas. This illumination level enables safe movement and wayfinding during fire emergencies when normal lighting may fail. This numerical standard is critical for life safety compliance. Emergency lighting must maintain 10 lux minimum per PEC Part 7; this is a foundational life safety numerical standard.

questions.text: What is the correct LEA response to a building energy-performance question?

options.text: Use RA 11285 with the DOE Guidelines for new construction, retrofits, lighting, controls, daylighting, and envelope OTTV.
Use only the plumbing code because energy performance is a drainage issue.
Use only Spanish colonial planning rules because orientation affects solar gain.
Use no statutory source because energy conservation is optional.

questions.rationale: Use RA 11285 with the DOE Guidelines for new construction, retrofits, lighting, controls, daylighting, and envelope OTTV. RA 11285 and the DOE Guidelines are the checked source families for building energy performance.
